metrics.name: follow_up_questions
metrics.title: Follow-up questions
metrics.evidence: Most questions dig into specific parts of the output: the cascade delete bug, a quoted line on the cohort query and parser, a quoted line on loading at startup ('is this proposed or existing functionality?'), why the module is named after the types file instead of being exported as schemas.py, and whether the tests are new or moved from backend.

metrics.name: coding_guidelines
metrics.title: Coding guidelines
metrics.evidence: The coding, git, Python and project CLAUDE.md guidelines were in context and the commit subjects follow the conventional form (for example test(schema): cover model validators), but JAVASCRIPT_CODING_PRACTICE.md, which covers the changed .github/workflows/test-integration.js, never reached context.

metrics.name: prompt_granularity
metrics.title: Prompt granularity
metrics.evidence: 13 of 50 prompts produced output, with a median of 24 generated lines each (band 3 is below 50), mostly 'y' approvals of single plan steps; only the /plan-issue prompt went past 200 lines (218).
